title: Political claim check: was Centre capital expenditure 'cut' in 2025-26?

verification_claim.text: The Centre cut capital expenditure in 2025-26, and Centre capex fell from 3.2% of GDP in 2024-25 to 3.1% in 2025-26.

definitions: A reduction from Budget Estimate (BE) to Revised Estimate (RE) is a cut relative to the original budget plan.
A year-on-year change compares one year's realised/revised level with the preceding year's level.
Nominal rupee expenditure and expenditure as a share of GDP can move in different directions.

evidence.title: This is a budget without an economic strategy, an economic statesmanship
evidence.evidence_summary: P. Chidambaram's published Congress commentary argues that 2025-26 capital expenditure was cut relative to the budget plan and that Centre capex fell from 3.2% to 3.1% of GDP.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
evidence.title: Budget at a Glance 2026-27 — Trend in Capital Expenditure
evidence.evidence_summary: The official chart shows Centre capital expenditure of about ₹10.5 lakh crore in 2024-25 and about ₹11.0 lakh crore in RE 2025-26. As a share of GDP, the chart shows 3.2% in 2024-25 and 3.1% in RE 2025-26.

evidence.publisher: Ministry of Finance, Government of India
evidence.title: Budget at a Glance 2025-26
evidence.evidence_summary: The original BE 2025-26 placed total capital expenditure at ₹11.2109 lakh crore, which is above the later RE level of roughly ₹11.0 lakh crore.

research_summary: The claim mixes two different comparisons. Relative to the original 2025-26 Budget Estimate, the later Revised Estimate is lower, so describing a cut versus the budget plan is supportable. However, nominal Centre capex still rose from about ₹10.5 lakh crore in 2024-25 to about ₹11.0 lakh crore in RE 2025-26. At the same time, capex as a share of GDP declined from 3.2% to 3.1%. Saying simply that 'capex fell' without specifying the comparison is therefore misleading.

locked_claims.text: Centre capital expenditure was about ₹10.5 lakh crore in 2024-25.
Centre capital expenditure was about ₹11.0 lakh crore in RE 2025-26.
The original BE 2025-26 capital expenditure was ₹11.2109 lakh crore.
Centre capex as a share of GDP moved from 3.2% in 2024-25 to 3.1% in RE 2025-26.

material_caveats: The cut is relative to the original 2025-26 Budget Estimate, not a year-on-year fall in nominal rupee capital expenditure.
Nominal Centre capex rose year-on-year from about ₹10.5 lakh crore to about ₹11.0 lakh crore.
Capex as a share of GDP did decline from 3.2% to 3.1%.
prohibited_claims: Centre capital expenditure fell in absolute rupee terms from 2024-25 to 2025-26.
There was no cut of any kind in 2025-26 capital expenditure.
The political claim is wholly false.
The political claim is wholly correct without qualification.
